![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `validateSpec` method runs on the raw spec object *before* the formal spec validation seam (`validateSpec`) is executed. If the spec is partially filled or contains optional/missing fields (e.g., `items` with missing labels, or a missing `footerItem` label), accessing properties directly like `item.label` or `spec.footerItem.label` can throw a `TypeError` and crash the pipeline with a 500 error.

Using optional chaining and filtering the array to only include valid strings makes this check robust against unvalidated inputs.

```suggestion
    const textsToCheck = [
      spec.title,
      ...(spec.items ?? []).map((item) => item?.label),
      spec.footerItem?.label,
      spec.dedication
    ].filter((text): text is string => typeof text === 'string');
```

**suggestion:** Exposing which field triggered the violation would make this error more actionable.

Currently callers only see a generic error and static `details`. Since you’re already iterating each text segment, you could tag or capture the offending segment (e.g., `title`, `item #1`, `footer`) and surface that in `details` or the message. That lets clients and tests identify exactly which spec segment violated policy without changing `SafetyPolicyResult`’s shape.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recreate base safety mock after restoreAllMocks**

In this test file, `afterEach` calls `vi.restoreAllMocks()` at line 34, but `baseDeps` is created once for the whole `describe`; after the first generate-pipeline test, this new `checkContentSafety` mock loses its `mockReturnValue({ ok: true })`, so later tests call it and get `undefined`, causing `runGeneratePipeline` to throw at `safetyResult.ok` before exercising the intended branches. Rebuild these deps in `beforeEach`/per test or reapply the mock implementation after restores so `npm test` stays green.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include styleHint in the safety gate**

When a request has a clean spec but a disallowed keyword in `styleHint`, this gate still returns ok because it only checks `parsedInput.data.spec`; the same `styleHint` is then passed to prompt assembly at lines 83-85 and inserted verbatim into the provider prompt by `prompt-assembly.adapter.ts`, so content like `styleHint: 'self-harm scene'` can still reach image generation despite this new safety gate. Extend the checked input to cover `styleHint` before assembling the prompt.
